title: General Knowledge Quiz #9 | 50 Questions Everyone Should Know

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.reveal: Not Sydney, not Melbourne. Canberra was built as the ultimate COMPROMISE!

questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.reveal: Eight legs and zero chill.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.reveal: Not Mercury! Venus traps its heat under a thick blanket of clouds.

questions.question: What is the largest mammal on Earth?
questions.reveal: Its heart alone can weigh around 180 kilograms. Big heart, BIGGER whale!

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.reveal: Peak trivia, right there.

questions.question: Which country has the largest population in the world?
questions.reveal: India overtook China in 2023. Did that one catch you out?

questions.question: How many minutes are in a full day?
questions.reveal: Twenty-four times sixty, people!

questions.question: What language is spoken in Brazil?
questions.reveal: Not Spanish! Brazil is the BIGGEST Portuguese-speaking country on the planet.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.reveal: Holy guacamole, that was an easy one.

questions.question: In which city would you find the Colosseum?
questions.reveal: When in Rome, answer like the Romans.

questions.question: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.reveal: The ONLY even prime. Odd, isn't it?

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.reveal: Four chambers, one very busy pump.

questions.question: How many players from each team are on the court in netball?
questions.reveal: Seven a side, and every one of them has a set position.

questions.question: What is the bee that lays all the eggs in a hive called?
questions.reveal: Long live the queen BEE!

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.reveal: One small step for man, one giant leap for your score.

questions.question: At what temperature in degrees Celsius does water boil at sea level?
questions.reveal: Perfect timing for a cuppa.

questions.question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.reveal: It lives in your ear and is smaller than a grain of rice.

questions.question: Which country is famous for its tulips and windmills?
questions.reveal: Tulip if you got that one right.

questions.question: What is the longest river in Australia?
questions.reveal: Over 2,500 kilometres of it.

questions.question: Which author wrote Pride and Prejudice?
questions.reveal: A truth universally acknowledged: Austen is a LEGEND.

questions.question: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow paint?
questions.reveal: Easy being green on this one.

questions.question: What is the fastest bird in the world?
questions.reveal: It can top 300 km/h in a dive. Zoom!

questions.question: In which country would you find Machu Picchu?
questions.reveal: Llama tell you, the views are INCREDIBLE.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.reveal: Not So! Na comes from its Latin name, natrium.

questions.question: How many days are in a leap year?
questions.reveal: One bonus day every four years. Lucky us!

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.reveal: Closest, but NOT the hottest. Sneaky, right?

questions.question: What colourful puzzle cube was invented by Ernő Rubik in 1974?
questions.reveal: Bet you can't solve it in under ten seconds.

questions.question: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
questions.reveal: Our neighbour to the west.

questions.question: Which fruit wears its seeds on the outside?
questions.reveal: Around 200 seeds on every berry. Berry impressive.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.reveal: Peace at last.

questions.question: Which reptile is famous for changing the colour of its skin?
questions.reveal: Myth-bust: it's mostly about mood and temperature, not hiding!

questions.question: Who painted The Starry Night?
questions.reveal: Painted from his window, and still a STAR.

questions.question: What is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.reveal: It covers about one ninth of all the land on Earth.

questions.question: How many continents are there?
questions.reveal: Seven continents, one very round planet.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.reveal: Not the chocolate bar, although we wouldn't say no.

questions.question: Which gas makes party balloons float?
questions.reveal: Bonus points if you said it in a squeaky voice.

questions.question: In which sport would you hit a shuttlecock?
questions.reveal: The fastest racket sport on Earth. Smashing!

questions.question: What is Big Ben in London?
questions.reveal: Myth-bust: the tower is called the Elizabeth Tower. Big Ben is the BELL inside!

questions.question: What is the square root of 144?
questions.reveal: A dozen, if you're feeling fancy.

questions.question: Which Australian bird is famous for its laughing call?
questions.reveal: Laughing all the way to the gum tree.

questions.question: What was the name of Captain Cook's ship when he reached Australia's east coast in 1770?
questions.reveal: A very fitting name for that trip.

questions.question: What is a word that sounds the same as another but has a different meaning?
questions.reveal: Like sea and see. Did you hear that one coming?

questions.question: Which planet has the most known moons?
questions.reveal: More than 270 and counting. Moon-believable!

questions.question: What creature appears on the flag of Wales?
questions.reveal: Wales doesn't do boring flags.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your body make when your skin is in sunlight?
questions.reveal: The sunshine vitamin. Slip, slop, slap first though!

questions.question: Which city hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics?
questions.reveal: Aussie, Aussie, Aussie! Oi, oi, oi!

questions.question: What type of pasta is shaped like little bow ties?
questions.reveal: Farfalle means BUTTERFLIES in Italian.

questions.question: What do you call a word made by rearranging the letters of another word?
questions.reveal: Listen and silent. Mind blown?

questions.question: What is the driest non-polar desert in the world?
questions.reveal: Some weather stations there have never recorded rain.

questions.question: Legend says a falling apple inspired which scientist's theory of gravity?
questions.reveal: The apple didn't fall far from the genius.
